subject: Dedicated capacity: OptiSoft sizing recap & pricing targets
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@optisoft.com>, Tom Lee <tom.lee@optisoft.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T15:23:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity: OptiSoft sizing recap & pricing targets

Hi Emma / Tom — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the numbers we discussed so we have an aligned starting point for pricing and the technical follow-up.

Call highlights (short):
- Workload: user-facing assistant for support + lightweight summarization for internal agents.
- Target latency: 95th perc <= 300ms for short prompts (<=512 tokens); burst tolerance for longer runs (up to ~2s).
- Desired SLA: reserved capacity with predictable throughput, can tolerate occasional fallbacks to smaller model family.

Key numbers we captured (please flag if anything looks off):
- Production target: ~1.2 billion generated tokens / month (this is after post-processing and includes retries).
- Peak concurrent inference: ~18-22 concurrent streams (spikes to ~30 for 10–15 minutes/day).
- Typical request mix: 70% short chat (avg 300 tokens generated), 30% longer (>1k tokens) for Summarize/Agent flows.
- Acceptance budget range (you mentioned on call): $100–$150 per 1M tokens effective target.

Preliminary capacity envelope (engineering back-of-envelope):
- Candidate GPU: NVIDIA H100 80GB (preferred for long-context summarization) — 1x H100 can sustain ~45–60 generated tokens/sec for the model family you mentioned at 2K context with our optimized runtime.
- Estimated reserved footprint: 3 x H100 to hit steady-state with headroom for bursts and rolling maintenance. That maps to an estimated effective unit economics in the $95–$140 / 1M tokens band depending on utilization and caching.

Attachments: I attached a short estimate (redwood-dedicated-pricing-estimate.xlsx) with two sizing scenarios (conservative / optimized) and a one-page mutual action plan (optiSoft-muth-action-plan.pdf).

Next steps / asks from your side:
1) Confirm the monthly token target (is 1.2B the right baseline or should we model 2B as a high-growth case?).
2) Share a short sample of request size distribution if you can (histogram or even a small CSV) — helps us tune batching and cache assumptions.
3) Are there procurement constraints (PO timeline, required SOW language, security/compliance docs) we should prep for?

I'll loop in our infra lead (Marissa) on the technical sizing once you confirm the traffic profile; we can set a 30–45 min deep-dive next week to lock the GPU mix and SLA/commit pricing.

Thanks — Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-11-21T09:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: OptiSoft sizing recap & pricing targets

Thanks Sean — very helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side:

Numbers (confirmed):
- Baseline prod: 1.2B generated tokens / month (this excludes embeddings and analytics).
- Upside scenario: plan for 1.9–2.2B / month if we onboard two more product regions next quarter.
- Active users: ~420k monthly active, average usage ~3 prompts/day, ~600 tokens generated per prompt on average (that aligns with your 300 vs 1k split because of mixed flows).
- Procurement: we typically need a standard PO + signed SOW; Finance will require a 30–45 day net payment term.
- Security: we'll need SOC2 Type II evidence and an IP/data segregation note for the private tenant.

Budget: we are targeting ~ $125 / 1M tokens effective. That’s our internal hurdle; if reserved capacity gets us below $120 / 1M tokens we can accelerate decisioning.

Scheduling: Tom and I are available for a technical sizing on Tue 2026-11-30 10:00–11:00 PT if that works for you and Marissa.

Thanks — Emma
Emma Jones
Head of Infrastructure & AI Ops | OptiSoft
emma.jones@optisoft.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity: OptiSoft sizing recap & pricing targets

Looping you both on Emma's clarified numbers. Quick internal notes / numbers I pulled from the pricing workbook:

- Baseline (1.2B tokens/mo) conservative config:
  * 3 x H100 80GB reserved (24/7) + 1 hot spare in cluster for maintenance 
  * Estimated monthly infra + infra ops pass-through: $148k/mo 
  * Effective cost at 70% utilization: ~$176 / 1M tokens (too high vs their target)

- Optimized (with prefix/KV caching and aggressive batching) scenario:
  * 3 x H100 with runtime cache and request coalescing, plus spot burst pool for peak (up to 1 additional H100 equivalent)
  * Estimated monthly: $108k/mo
  * Effective cost at 85% utilization: ~$95–$110 / 1M tokens (falls into their target band)

- Key levers to hit $125 / 1M: improve hit-rate on prefix cache (we should ask for representative prompt set), commit to a 12-mo reserved term to reduce unit infra cost, and limit peak SLA window for long-context jobs (route long jobs to a separate pool or allow slightly higher p95).

Action items for commercial:
- Sean: confirm whether OptiSoft is willing to consider a 12-mo reserved term vs 6-mo trial. That impacts list vs net pricing materially.
- Vivek: can we pre-authorize a 15% discount for a 12-mo commit if they agree to an initial PO within 30 days?

Attachments: I updated the spreadsheet with the optimized scenario and a short MAM (mutual-action) PDF — attaching as redwood-dedicated-pricing-estimate.xlsx and optiSoft-muth-action-plan.pdf.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@optisoft.com>, Tom Lee <tom.lee@optisoft.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: OptiSoft sizing recap & pricing targets

Emma / Tom — thanks for the clarifications and the budget range. Short answers and next steps: 

1) Term & pricing: based on Marissa's optimized model, we can meet an effective $110 / 1M tokens with a 12‑month reserved commitment (3 x H100 reserved, runtime caching turned on). I'll flag that as our target commercial offer. We can draft two options for the SOW: a 12-mo reserved at preferred pricing and a 6-mo pilot with a slightly higher unit rate.

2) SOC2 + security: I'll start the SOC2 evidence pack and the private-tenant segregation note; expect an email with links to the artifacts by EOD Monday.

3) Technical deep-dive: Tue 2026-11-30 10:00 PT works for us — sending a calendar invite and a short agenda (model family, sample traffic, caching expectations, fallback policies).

4) Procurement timeline: if OptiSoft can sign a PO within 30 days of SOW finalization we can lock the 12-mo pricing band and pre-schedule capacity. If Finance needs 45-day net, we can still proceed but will need to finalize payment terms in the SOW addendum.

Action items we own this week:
- Marissa: finalize the optimized pricing worksheet and call out sensitivity to utilization (attachment updated).
- Commercial: I will prepare two SOW drafts and an indicative DocuSign for quick review.
- Ops: bundle SOC2 evidence and private-tenant segregation note and share link.

Emma/Tom — can you confirm the 30-day PO cadence and whether OptiSoft is open to a 12-mo committed term? If yes, we’ll prioritize the 12-mo SOW + DocuSign route so we can hit the $110 / 1M effective target.

Thanks — Sean
